The build passes. The acceptance test suite exercised the new path — the debug log shows `Duplicate owner email at POST /api/owners: An owner with email 'owner5@example.test' already exists` producing a 409.

## Summary

I implemented owner-creation rejection when the lower-cased email is already used by another owner, returning **409 Conflict**, by mirroring the existing telephone-uniqueness design so no single class became a catch-all:

- **`OwnerRepository.findByEmail`** — new query method, with implementations in all three repository backends:
  - `JpaOwnerRepositoryImpl` (JPQL), `SpringDataOwnerRepository` (`@Query`), and `JdbcOwnerRepositoryImpl` (named-param SQL).
- **`ClinicService.findOwnerByEmail`** + **`ClinicServiceImpl`** — read-only service pass-through, matching `findOwnerByTelephone`.
- **`OwnerEmailUniquenessValidator`** (new `@Component`) — single-responsibility check; skips a `null` email since email is optional, and throws on a match.
- **`DuplicateOwnerEmailException`** (new) — the domain signal for the conflict.
- **`ExceptionControllerAdvice`** — new handler mapping the exception to 409 with an `errors: ["email"]` body, consistent with the telephone/household handlers.
- **`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`** — injects the validator and calls `validateUnique(owner.getEmail())` right after telephone validation. Email is already normalized (lower-cased) upstream via `EmailNormalizer.normalize`, so comparison happens on the canonical stored form — two emails differing only in case are treated as duplicates.

Since email is optional, absent emails are never treated as duplicates.
